intro.title: Lists keep values in order
intro.body: Index from 0, use len() for the count, and append() to add to the end. Lists can hold any mix of values.

challenges.prompt: Add 9 to the end of the list.
challenges.explanation: list.append(value) adds one value to the end.

challenges.prompt: Match each expression with its result.
challenges.explanation: len counts, indexing picks, sum adds, and + joins lists.

challenges.prompt: There is an off-by-one error. Tap the line and choose the fix.
challenges.explanation: Indices run 0 to len(nums) - 1, so the range must stop at len(nums).

challenges.prompt: Read n followed by n numbers and print the largest one.

starterCode.python:
n = int(input())
nums = list(map(int, input().split()))
# print the largest value

challenges.explanation: start with nums[0] and replace it whenever a bigger value appears, or use max(nums).
